issues.failure_explanation: The area argument chooses a in the plane, not in supp(μ), so the defining minimum does not imply the displayed inequality. The lower bound is genuinely false under the stated assumptions. Let μ be normalized arclength on the unit circle together with a circle centered at 3 of radius ℓ=e^(−n²), and let S consist of n rotated equally spaced unit-circle nodes and one node on the tiny circle. The regularity constants can be uniform with α=β=1, KS=O(1/n), and ε comparable to 1/n. The potential range tends to log 3. Nevertheless, all Lagrange sup-norms on this support remain bounded: the unit-circle cardinal factors are bounded there, while values on the tiny component contain a factor O(ℓ3^n). Thus the left side of the claimed lower bound tends to zero, not log 3.
